hero.roleLine: Human-centered AI researcher and research-tool builder
hero.lede: I study how people evaluate, trust, audit, and govern generative AI — and I build the interfaces and research infrastructure needed to collect those judgments at scale.
hero.context: PhD candidate in Computer Science at The George Washington University.

researchProfile.label: Research
researchProfile.value: Human-centered evaluation, AI auditing, trust, privacy, and governance of generative AI.

researchProfile.label: Methods
researchProfile.value: Interactive experiments, large-scale online studies, interviews, surveys, qualitative analysis, and mixed methods.

researchProfile.label: Systems
researchProfile.value: Evaluation interfaces, auditing workflows, AI interaction-history dashboards, study platforms, and human-data infrastructure.

researchProfile.label: Currently
researchProfile.value: PhD candidate in Computer Science at The George Washington University, advised by Adam Aviv.

projectsPage.lede: Each project combines research design with systems I built to run it. Together they cover human evaluation and auditing, research infrastructure, privacy and interaction histories, and workplace adoption and governance.

publicationsPage.lede: Peer-reviewed and preprint work on generative AI evaluation and auditing, measurement of user perceptions, and privacy transparency. My earlier work on privacy labels runs directly into my current focus: how people and institutions evaluate the systems they are asked to trust.

cvPage.lede: My CV covers education, publications, research experience, systems I have built, and technical skills.
cvPage.summary: PhD candidate in Computer Science (usable security and privacy; trustworthy AI) at The George Washington University. I work on human-centered evaluation and auditing of generative AI, privacy, and AI governance, and I build the study platforms and interfaces that make that research possible.
